title: Farm Growth Topped 4% for a Decade, Modi Tells Kisan Tak Conference
excerpt: Addressing the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference in New Delhi, the Prime Minister credited a decade of above-4% farm growth with helping 50 crore people defeat poverty, and urged crop diversification and natural farming.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi said India's agriculture sector has grown at an average of over 4% a year over the past decade — the first time since Independence, he said — in an address at the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on November 12.
  • Citing a World Bank study, Modi said nearly 50 crore people have defeated poverty over the past 12 to 13 years, with many of them small farmers and agricultural workers and a rapid fall in rural poverty.
  • He said India now exports more than Rs 4 lakh crore of agricultural products a year, and that the government has disbursed Rs 16 lakh crore in fertiliser subsidies over the decade to shield farmers from global price shocks.
  • His forward ask to farmers was diversification: shift crops, adopt natural farming and reduce chemical use.

India's farm sector has recorded average annual growth of over 4% over the past decade, Prime Minister Narendra Modi told an agriculture conference in New Delhi on Thursday — a rate he said the country has not sustained since Independence. Speaking at the plenary session of the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference, organised by the India Today Group at Bharat Mandapam, Modi credited that growth as the primary engine behind a fall in poverty, and set out diversification and natural farming as the sector's next task.

The claims in the address

Citing a World Bank study, Modi said nearly 50 crore Indians have escaped poverty over the past 12 to 13 years, many of them small farmers and agricultural workers, with rural poverty falling rapidly, The CSR Journal reported. He said India exports over Rs 4 lakh crore of agricultural products annually, helping raise farmers' incomes, and pointed to India's standing as the world's largest producer of milk, pulses, jute and rice, and the second-largest producer of wheat, cotton, fruits, vegetables and fish. These are the Prime Minister's figures, stated in his address; this article reports them as claims from the speech rather than independently compiled statistics.

"These are the Prime Minister's figures, stated in his address; this article reports them as claims from the speech rather than independently compiled statistics."

The ask: diversify and farm naturally

The policy direction in the speech was toward how farming is done. Modi urged farmers to diversify crops and adopt natural farming and reduce chemical use, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. He also joked that because the media is least interested in farming topics and more interested in controversies, he would provide them with some headlines — a remark that framed the growth and poverty figures as the headlines he wanted carried.

Context

The address came at a two-day conference on the theme "Smart Kisan, Viksit Bharat," and followed scientific sessions at the same meeting where researchers warned that more than half of India's fertiliser never feeds the crop — context that sits alongside the Prime Minister's call to cut chemical use. What to watch is whether the diversification and natural-farming push is followed by named schemes, budgets or state-level targets; the address itself announced the direction, not a new program.
